Good, about the hunt not about the stupid debate.

Legal hunts like this are a huge net benefit to wildlife conservation and elephant populations. The major threats to elephant populations are habitat loss and poaching both of which are mitigated by legal hunting. The money paid by hunters pays for private game reserves that massively increase the total land area of protected habitat of both the game animals and all the other wildlife. It also pays salaries to people who would otherwise be desperately poor and have both the skills and opportunities to become poachers. These are very poor countries especially in these rural regions and a elephant tusks are worth tens of thousands of dollars. Both the laws managing game animal populations and the profit motives of the game reserve owners mitigate against overhunting that would threaten long term survival of the herds.

This is not theory... it's borne out by the statistics. Countries with legal hunting have generally seen population increases as private land owners maintain existing and start new game ranches while countries like Kenya that have banned big game hunting have seen population declines as private land owners convert to cattle ranching. This is why many conservation groups support trophy hunting as one component in conservation policy and most others don't oppose it.
